t:
(a) Authority to Provide Support.—The Secretary of Defense may provide financial or non-monetary support to qualified nonprofit organizations in order to assist such organizations in carrying out programs to support the attendance at a camp, or camp-like setting, of children of military families who have experienced the death of a family member or other loved one or who have another family member living with a substance use disorder or post-traumatic stress disorder. 
    (b) Application for Support.—
        (1) In general.—Each organization seeking support pursuant to subsection (a) shall submit to the Secretary of Defense an application therefor containing such information as the Secretary shall specify for purposes of this section. 
        (2) Contents.—Each application submitted under paragraph (1) shall include the following:
            (A) A description of the program for which support is being sought, including the location of the setting or settings under the program, the duration of such setting or settings, any local partners participating in or contributing to the program, and the ratio of counselors, trained volunteers, or both to children at such setting or settings. 
            (B) An estimate of the number of children of military families to be supported using the support sought. 
            (C) A description of the type of activities that will be conducted using the support sought, including the manner in which activities are particularly supportive to children of military families described in subsection (a). 
            (D) A description of the outreach conducted or to be conducted by the organization to military families regarding the program.   
    (c) Use of Support.—Support provided by the Secretary of Defense to an organization pursuant to subsection (a) shall be used by the organization to support attendance at a camp, or camp-like setting, of children of military families described in subsection (a).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that nonprofit organizations (outside parties) interact with the Secretary of Defense and that "local partners participating" signals participation. But the only interaction is an application for financial or non-monetary support, which the definition expressly excludes as an application for benefits or grants. Nothing requires consultation, comment, hearings, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue before a federal decision.
fable.s: Each organization seeking support pursuant to subsection (a) shall submit to the Secretary of Defense an application therefor containing such information as the Secretary shall specify for purposes of this section.

opus.w: The only outside parties here are nonprofits applying to the Secretary of Defense for financial or non-monetary support. Applying for grants or benefits is expressly excluded from participation. The phrase "local partners participating in or contributing to the program" refers to who runs the camp program. It does not set up consultation, comment, an advisory body, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: Each organization seeking support pursuant to subsection (a) shall submit to the Secretary of Defense an application therefor containing such information as the Secretary shall specify for purposes of this section.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes": nonprofit organizations submit material to the Secretary of Defense, and applications must list "local partners participating in" the program. That fails because this is an application for financial support, essentially a grant. The DEFINITION explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants. "Participating" here describes the camp program, not any role in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the process for nonprofit organizations to apply for financial support (grants) from the Secretary of Defense. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. Although outside entities are involved, their role is that of applicants seeking funding, not participants in a federal decision-making process through consultation, advisory boards, or public comment.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Application for Support.— (1) In general.—Each organization seeking support pursuant to subsection (a) shall submit to the Secretary of Defense an application therefor containing such information as the Secretary shall specify for purposes of this section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because nonprofit organizations (outside entities) are involved in the process, this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." This section describes the process for nonprofits to apply for financial support (grants) from the Secretary of Defense. The interaction is an application for funding, not a consultation or coordination on a federal decision-making process in the sense of advisory input or public comment on policy.
